name: Alcântara Space Center (CLA)
operator: Brazilian Air Force (with Brazilian Space Agency AEB)
expansion: Innospace HANBIT-Nano return to flight planned Nov 2026; Brazilian VLM-1 without date.
note: 2°S: best equatorial performance in the Americas; marketed as equatorial-to-polar (max inclination not published). US–Brazil Technology Safeguards Agreement 2019. First commercial orbital attempt (Innospace, Dec 2025) failed ~30 s after liftoff. Pad count estimated.

name: Andøya Spaceport
expansion: Second orbital pad in Norway's 2027 budget proposal (~NOK 650m, state-owned, leased to Andøya Space; MoD and Trade co-fund); tenant not named. Astrobotic Xodiac (reusable test vehicle, not orbital) term sheet Aug 2025, campaigns from 2026.
isar_access: Exclusive pad (Orbital Launch Pad A) for up to 20 years since April 2021; Spectrum F1 failed 30 Mar 2025, F2 reached orbit 5 Sep 2026
note: Licence for the whole spaceport: 30 launches a year, at most 4 at night; headings 280–360°. The only orbital pad is Isar-exclusive, so future tenants share the 30/yr licence. Team information: further operators want to launch from 2027/28; public sources (Oct 2026) name none signed (RFA's 2020 pad deal went dormant when it moved to SaxaVord; Astrobotic Xodiac is not orbital). Owned 90% by the Norwegian state, 10% Kongsberg. Ships in the hazard zone caused the 25 Mar 2026 abort.

name: Arnhem Space Centre
expansion: ELA gave up the lease after a 2024 dispute with the Northern Land Council and announced a move to Weipa (QLD); company reported in liquidation.
note: Only three NASA suborbital sounding rockets (2022). Not a realistic orbital option. inclination_min = site latitude (computed).

name: Atlantic Spaceport Complex (St. Lawrence, Newfoundland)
expansion: SLC-01 with two orbital pads in Phase 2 construction (Oct 2026), orbital NET 2028 for light (Tundra) and medium (Tempest) vehicles; DND facility-access deal reported Oct 2026 (not opened).
note: Coordinates estimated (town of St. Lawrence). Operator claims 'widest range of inclinations in Canada' (no figures); polar_sso inferred from southward ocean corridor. Taiga suborbital not yet flown (two aborted attempts Aug 2025).

name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
operator: Roscosmos (leased by Russia from Kazakhstan to 2050)
expansion: Baiterek (Site 45) for Soyuz-5/Sunkar: suborbital first test 30 Apr 2026, orbital flights to follow; Site 31/6 damaged 27 Nov 2025, restored Mar 2026; Proton-M to be replaced by Angara A5
note: Coords = Site 31/6 (Soyuz). Pads est.: 31/6, 81/24 + 200/39 (Proton), 45/1 (Baiterek). Inclinations observed 2015–26 (GCAT); 51.6° is the lowest without overflying China. Super-heavy only historically (Energia 1987–88). Lease US$115m/yr.

name: Biak Spaceport (planned)
expansion: BRIN seeking National Strategic Project status; legal/regulatory work from 2026, technical development afterwards; China and Russia have expressed investment interest
note: Near-equatorial site in Papua; feasibility studies done but no construction or partner confirmed. Access model (sovereign vs foreign partner) undecided, hence null. Exact coordinates not published.

name: Bowen Orbital Spaceport (Abbot Point)
expansion: Eris TestFlight 2 targeted end-2026; Eris Block 2 (up to 1,000 kg LEO) in development.
note: Australia's first licensed commercial orbital spaceport (5 Mar 2024). Eris TestFlight 1 (30 Jul 2025) failed after 14 s. Low/mid inclinations only (operator 20–65°). Coordinates estimated from a Maritime Safety Queensland notice seen in search, not opened.

name: Luigi Broglio Space Centre (San Marco), Malindi
expansion: Reactivation for START-1 studied by ASI; no current project
note: Offshore San Marco platform: 9 Scout orbital launches 1967-1988 (GCAT). Ground station still tracks ASI, ESA, NASA and Chinese missions. Equatorial location.

name: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station
operator: U.S. Space Force (Space Launch Delta 45, Eastern Range)
active_vehicles: Atlas V (United Launch Alliance), Falcon 9 (Block 5) (SpaceX), New Glenn (Blue Origin), Vulcan Centaur (United Launch Alliance)
planned_vehicles: Alpha (Firefly Aerospace), Daytona (Phantom Space), Nova (Pathfinder) (Stoke Space), Starship / Super Heavy (SpaceX), Terran R (Relativity Space)
providers: Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Phantom Space, Relativity Space, SpaceX, Stoke Space, United Launch Alliance
orbits: escape, GEO, GTO, LEO, lunar, MEO, SSO
expansion: SLC-37 Starship pads (under construction); LC-14 Stoke Nova (pad ~complete, first flight early 2027); LC-16 Relativity Terran R (target late 2026, likely 2027); SLC-20 leased to Firefly (inactive); SLC-13 Phantom/Vaya and SLC-15 ABL allocated 2023; LC-36 New Glenn damaged May 2026.
note: Inclinations 28.5–58° computed from 37–114° azimuths (cos i = sin az · cos lat); SSO only via southern corridor with dogleg. Congestion: one main road, trucked methane. First attempt Vanguard TV3 1957 (background knowledge). No foreign launcher present.

name: Chabahar National Satellite Launch Base
expansion: Phase 1 declared complete Feb 2026 (ISA); Phase 2 to open to foreign satellites; full operation incl. international launches by end of Mar 2031
note: Coastal site on the Gulf of Oman, Iran's planned main spaceport. Phase 1 completion is an ISA claim; no launch confirmed as of Oct 2026. Coordinates from GCAT. Vehicle class and orbits not published.

name: Spaceport Cornwall (Cornwall Airport Newquay)
operator: Cornwall Airport Ltd (owned by Cornwall Council)
expansion: No orbital launch provider since Virgin Orbit's 2023 bankruptcy; talks with Sierra Space and a horizontal-launch provider reported (2023), nothing confirmed for 2024–2026.
note: Horizontal (air-launch) site: runway, no pad. Only orbital attempt was LauncherOne 'Start Me Up', 9 Jan 2023, failed. CAA spaceport licence Nov 2022. Irrelevant for a vertical launcher like Spectrum.

name: Djibouti spaceport (Obock, planned)
operator: Hong Kong Aerospace Technology (30-year management, then Djibouti)
expansion: USD 1bn site agreed in preliminary deal Jan 2023; completion 'as early as 2027'
note: Only a preliminary 2023 agreement found; no evidence of a formal contract or construction since. Treat as speculative.

name: East China Sea launch zone
operator: Sea-launch zone; operating launch centre not confirmed (Orienspace Gravity-1 flights)
note: New sea-launch zone in 2026: two Gravity-1 orbital launches (89° and 97.5°) per GCAT; no operator or capacity data found. Coordinates = GCAT launch point 2.

name: Esrange Space Center (Spaceport Esrange)
expansion: LC-3C pad in final construction for Firefly Alpha: 2 launches contracted, NET 2028 (Swedish national security + rideshare; FMV SEK 209m). LC-3A earmarked for Perigee Blue Whale 1 (2024 deal, slipped). LC-3B for reusable/lander tests.
isar_access: Engine test stands since 2020; second test site opened Feb 2026 (30+ engines/month, integrated stage acceptance)
note: Inclinations computed from 320–020° handbook sector; trajectories overfly Norway (Tromsø at 337°), so doglegs and Norwegian consent are live issues (CAA Norway report). SSC is wholly state-owned. RFA also tests engines here.

name: Etlaq Spaceport, Duqm
expansion: Full commercial operations targeted 2027 with multiple launch complexes; PLD Space Miura 5 second base (first flights from 2027); ABL MoU 2024; HyImpulse LoI Jun 2026
note: Middle East's first commercial spaceport; suborbital only so far (Duqm-1 Dec 2024; Duqm-2 aborted on pad). Open to foreign providers, a European competitor base. Coordinates from Wikipedia; GCAT lists 19.64N 57.68E. Orbit range not published.

name: German Offshore Spaceport (GOSA North Sea platform)
operator: German Offshore Spaceport Alliance (GOSA); OHB's European Spaceport Company (2026)
expansion: Ship-based platform (Combi Dock I, launchers 36–52 t). Federal funding ~€2.87m. In July 2026 OHB said the offshore concept continues but scope widened beyond the North Sea; Bundeswehr launch site under consideration (location open).
note: 2024 demo launches never flew; no German space law, so no licensing authority (govt answer Dec 2024). Environmental concerns (Dogger Bank, porpoises). Location not fixed, coordinates null.

name: Hainan Commercial Spaceport (Wenchang Commercial Space Launch Site)
operator: Hainan International Commercial Aerospace Launch Co. (HICAL)
active_vehicles: Long March 10B (CASC), Long March 12 (CASC), Long March 8 (CASC), Long March 8A (CASC)
planned_vehicles: Gravity-2 (Orienspace), Kinetica-2 (Lijian-2) (CAS Space), Nebula-1 (Deep Blue Aerospace), Pallas-1 (Galactic Energy), Tianlong-3 (Space Pioneer)
providers: CAS Space, CASC, Deep Blue Aerospace, Galactic Energy, Orienspace, Space Pioneer
expansion: Phase II pads 3 and 4 plus technical area due end-2026; future users listed: Tianlong-3, Pallas-1, Nebula-1, Gravity-2, Kinetica-2; sea-recovery vessel for reuse
note: China's first commercial spaceport, state JV (Hainan govt, CASC, CASIC, China SatNet). 1/9/14 launches 2024/25/26, mostly Guowang/Qianfan. CZ-10B: first Chinese orbital booster recovery (Jul 2026). Incl. observed 50–89°; SSO not yet flown.

name: Oriental Spaceport (Haiyang, Shandong; Yellow Sea sea launch)
operator: Oriental (DongFang) Spaceport under Taiyuan SLC jurisdiction, home port Haiyang
active_vehicles: Ceres-1 (Galactic Energy), Gravity-1 (Yinli-1) (Orienspace), Jielong-3 (Smart Dragon-3) (CASC), Long March 11 (CASC)
expansion: Local investment in liquid-fuel rocket technology and infrastructure (CGTN, 2026); public launch viewing
note: Sea-launch zone: rockets fly from ships/barges at varying Yellow Sea points (GCAT lists 8, 34–37°N); coords = LP4 off Haiyang. 25 offshore missions, 155 satellites by Jun 2026. Vehicles: CZ-11, Jielong-3, Ceres-1S, Gravity-1. Pads n/a.

name: Hammaguir (CIEES)
note: Historical French site: 4 Diamant A orbital launches 1965-67 incl. Asterix-1 (GCAT). Closed 1967; now an air base. Listed for completeness only.

name: Hokkaido Spaceport (HOSPO), Taiki
operator: SPACE COTAN (concession from Taiki Town since 1 Oct 2026)
expansion: LC-1 (pads LP11, LP12) construction completed 14 Oct 2026; LC-2 planned as shared govt/commercial pad for frequent launches; runway 1,300 m, 3,000 m studied
note: LC-1 done but no orbital vehicle ready: Interstellar ZERO first flight 2027 (Wikipedia). Open to foreign users: Japan subsidiary of a Taiwanese rocket firm launched there Jul 2025; Firefly in talks; MOU with Virginia Spaceport Oct 2026. Band estimated.

name: Taiwan National Launch Site (Jiupeng, Pingtung)
expansion: Site chosen 2025 in Jiupeng village, Manzhou; completion expected in the 2030s; Hsu-hai sounding-rocket complex opened 2025
note: Orbital site still in planning; coordinates are GCAT's existing Jiu Peng suborbital range (approximate for the new site). Meanwhile a Taiwanese developer's Japan subsidiary launched from HOSPO (Jul 2025).

name: Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center
operator: PLA Aerospace Force (Jiuquan SLC, Base 10); CASC listed as operator
active_vehicles: Ceres-1 (Galactic Energy), Ceres-2 (Galactic Energy), Hyperbola-1 (iSpace), Kinetica-1 (Lijian-1) (CAS Space), Kinetica-2 (Lijian-2) (CAS Space), Kuaizhou-11 (ExPace (CASIC)), Kuaizhou-1A (ExPace (CASIC)), Long March 12A (CASC), Long March 12B (CASC), Long March 2C (CASC), Long March 2D (CASC), Long March 2F (CASC), Long March 4B (CASC), Long March 4C (CASC), Pallas-1 (Galactic Energy), Tianlong-3 (Space Pioneer), Zhuque-2E (LandSpace), Zhuque-3 (LandSpace)
providers: CAS Space, CASC, ExPace (CASIC), Galactic Energy, iSpace, LandSpace, Space Pioneer
expansion: Dongfeng commercial test zone keeps adding private pads: Zhuque-3 (96B, 2025), CZ-12A/12B pad (2025), Pallas-1 pad (2026), Kinetica-2 (LC-140, 2026), Tianlong-3 (120B, 2026)
note: China's crewed (Shenzhou, 41.5°) and private-launcher hub: 21/34/27 orbital launches 2024/25/26. Inland: stages fall on land, enabling land booster landings (Zhuque-3, Aug 2026). Pads = 11 used since 2024 (est.). Heavy = CZ-12B ~20 t. ITAR bars US-content payloads.

name: Kennedy Space Center (LC-39)
active_vehicles: Falcon 9 (Block 5) (SpaceX), Falcon Heavy (SpaceX), Space Launch System (Block 1) (NASA)
expansion: LC-39A Starship pad (tower and launch mount installed; first Florida Starship NET late 2026); 39A now reserved for Falcon Heavy and Starship, Dragon moved to SLC-40 (2026).
note: Inclinations computed as for Cape Canaveral. Polar corridor so far used from SLC-40, not 39A. Artemis II (SLS) launched 1 Apr 2026 from 39B. No Falcon 9 from 39A since Dec 2025.

name: Pacific Spaceport Complex – Alaska (Kodiak)
expansion: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 4 (announced Jul 2026) for HASTE suborbital missile-defence flights under a US$266M USSF contract (12–18 launches to 2028); orbital Electron there only a possibility.
note: No orbital launch since Jan 2023 (ABL RS1, failed); Astra reached orbit 2021–22. Mostly MDA/USSF suborbital tests; 9 orbital missions since 1998. Remote: power, propellant, payload logistics. GCAT site code not given (likely KLC, unverified).

name: Guiana Space Centre (CSG), Kourou
planned_vehicles: Maia (MaiaSpace), Miura 5 (PLD Space), RFA One (Rocket Factory Augsburg), Sirius 13 (Sirius Space Services), Spectrum (Isar Aerospace), Vega E (Avio), Zephyr (Latitude)
providers: Arianespace, Avio, Isar Aerospace, Latitude, MaiaSpace, PLD Space, Rocket Factory Augsburg, Sirius Space Services
expansion: ELM-Diamant (ex-Diamant pad, CNES, €50m, build 2025–26): Isar, Latitude, PLD Space, RFA, Sirius Space (selected Apr 2026, replacing MaiaSpace). Ex-Soyuz ELS → ELM2 for MaiaSpace Maia (H2 2027). ELA-3 to be adapted for Vega-E.
isar_access: One of five ELM-Diamant laureates (term sheet 2022; still listed by CNES June 2026); no pad construction date announced
note: Reaches low inclinations and GTO as well as polar orbits Inclinations computed from azimuths (cos i = sin az·cos lat) at ELA-4; ESA cites a 102° launch sector. Usable pads: ELA-4 (Ariane 6), ELV (Vega C). Soyuz ended Feb 2022. Launches: 3 (2024), 7 (2025), 6 (2026 to Oct).

name: Kulasekarapattinam Spaceport (SSLV Launch Complex)
expansion: One SSLV pad; construction since 5 Mar 2025, budget Rs 985.96 crore; commissioning FY2026-27 (to Mar 2027); first launch targeted Dec 2026 (Wikipedia)
note: Built so small launchers reach polar/SSO directly without the Sriharikota dogleg. Inclination band is an estimate from the southward heading. Govt expects non-government light launchers to use it after commissioning (Parliament reply, Dec 2025).

name: Reagan Test Site, Kwajalein Atoll
operator: U.S. Army (US Army Garrison Kwajalein Atoll / Reagan Test Site)
expansion: None announced for orbital launch.
note: Near-equatorial US Army missile range. Hosted Falcon 1 (Omelek, 2006–09) and air-launched Pegasus; final Pegasus XL flew 3 Jul 2026 (LINK, 20.6°), so no active orbital user. Coordinates = Omelek pad. First year 2000 (Pegasus HETE-2) from background knowledge.

name: Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 (Māhia)
expansion: None announced; Rocket Lab growth goes to Neutron (Wallops LC-3) and Kodiak LC-4.
note: Private single-operator range (Electron only). Inclinations computed: 39° (latitude) to ~98° (SSO flown); Rocket Lab marketing reportedly claims down to ~30° with doglegs (not opened). 13/17/15 orbital launches 2024/25/26 (GCAT).

name: Naro Space Center
operator: KARI (Korea Aerospace Research Institute) under KASA
expansion: Private-company launch site, assembly and tracking facilities inside Naro being built in stages; Nuri 6th launch 2027; Hanwha Aerospace taking over Nuri technology (2025)
note: Korea's only orbital site. Nuri 4th (Nov 2025) and 5th (7 Oct 2026, 15 sats) succeeded, all to SSO. Band: Naro-1 80 deg (GCAT) to Nuri SSO. Private launchers (Innospace, Perigee) not yet flying orbital from Korea.

name: Ningbo International Commercial Launch Center (Xiangshan)
operator: Ningbo Commercial Aerospace Development Co. (local state firms, est. Jan 2026)
expansion: 2021 plan: CNY 20 bn, 67 km² (35 km² launch site), 100 satellites/yr, partner SAST; developer company formed Jan 2026, marine consulting tender Feb 2026
note: Coastal site in Xiangshan county, Zhejiang (~30°N); coordinates approximate (county), not a surveyed pad. Still in planning as of 2026; no first-launch date published.

name: Spaceport Nova Scotia (Canso)
expansion: Isar dedicated Spectrum complex (pad handover due 1 Nov 2026, more infrastructure by end-2027, first launch 2028); RDX Aurora-8 on exclusive third pad (~Q3 2028); Innospace HANBIT LOI (Mar 2026); fourth pad site identified.
isar_access: Facilities usage agreement signed 7 Jul 2026: dedicated Spectrum complex, 10 years + 2×5-year options, US$3.75M per quarter (30-month fee waiver after year 1), first orbital launch 2028.
note: First launch planned 2028. Up to 40 launches a year by 2029 (target); inclination range as claimed by the operator Inclinations 45.1–98.1° as published by MLS (98.1 SSO, 87.9 polar). Only suborbital flights so far (Barracuda, below Kármán line). Cyclone-4M plan (8/yr) dropped 2024. Canada–US TSA not addressed in the Isar release.

name: Palmachim Airbase
operator: Israeli Air Force / Israel Space Agency
note: Retrograde-only to avoid overflying Israel and neighbours, costing payload. Band = achieved 2016-25 (GCAT; ~143 deg historically). Only Shavit/Ofeq military launches, roughly one every 2-3 years (2016, 2020, 2023, Sep 2025).

name: Plesetsk Cosmodrome
operator: Russian Aerospace Forces (VKS), Ministry of Defence
expansion: Angara-1.2/A5 from Site 35/1 take over from retired Soyuz-2.1v (last flight Feb 2025) and Rokot
note: Military site at 63°N for high-inclination, Molniya and SSO payloads; stages fall over Arctic. Busiest Russian site in 2025–26 (9 and 8 launches). Inclinations observed 2015–26 (GCAT). Closed to foreign/commercial customers.

name: Manuel Belgrano Space Center (Puerto Belgrano)
expansion: Tronador II national launcher, first orbital flight target 2030.
note: Coordinates estimated (naval base). Long-delayed national programme; tests from Punta Indio. Polar capability inferred from Tronador II's polar-orbit payload spec.

name: Santa Maria Spaceport (Malbusca Launch Centre), Azores
expansion: Innospace (KR) site agreement Jan 2026 for Hanbit rockets, operations to 2030, first launch targeted 2026 (no launch reported); first orbital attempts projected 2027. Suborbital first (SpaceForest Perun). ESA Space Rider landing site.
note: ANACOM licence (Aug 2025, 5 yrs) covers site operation only; each launch needs its own licence. Coordinates approximate (37°N 25°W). Orbital azimuths not published. Only EU-territory candidate at mid latitude.

name: SaxaVord Spaceport
planned_vehicles: RFA One (Rocket Factory Augsburg), Skyrora XL (Skyrora)
expansion: Two more launch complexes under construction. RFA One maiden flight from Pad Fredo slipped after a vehicle issue in late July 2026 (no new date). Skyrora XL multi-launch agreement (2021), XL first flight expected 2027. Orbex Prime cancelled (Feb 2026).
note: Licensed and range-licensed (Apr 2024) but no orbital launch yet. Only pad is RFA-exclusive, so other launchers (e.g. Skyrora) lack a pad. Inclinations computed from 330–030°. Lockheed/ABL Pathfinder plan dropped.

name: Semnan Space Center / Imam Khomeini Space Launch Terminal
operator: Iranian Space Agency (vehicles by Ministry of Defence)
active_vehicles: Simorgh (Iranian Space Agency), Zuljanah (Iran Ministry of Defence)
providers: Iran Ministry of Defence, Iranian Space Agency
note: Band = achieved 2008-24 (GCAT), never polar. Simorgh complex struck 24-26 Mar 2026 (Wikipedia citing IISS); Safir/Zoljanah pad reportedly undamaged. Last attempt Zoljanah Sep 2025 (failed). Sanctions rule out Western use.

name: Shahroud Space Center
note: Military solid-fuel site (Qased, Qaem-100). Band = achieved 2020-23 (GCAT). Single pad reported largely destroyed in strikes 6-10 Mar 2026 (Wikipedia citing IISS), so marked inactive; rebuild possible. Last orbital launch Sep 2024.

name: Sohae Satellite Launching Station
operator: NATA (National Aerospace Technology Administration, formerly NADA)
expansion: Major upgrade and expansion completed per Apr 2026 imagery; new structures May 2026; site >6 km2
note: Reconnaissance-satellite launches under UN sanctions; no foreign access. Band = achieved 2016-24 (GCAT). Last attempt 27 May 2024 (new kerolox LV, first-stage explosion). Pads: LC1 gantry (Unha-3), LC2 coastal (Chollima-1).

name: Turkish spaceport in Somalia
expansion: Phase 1 (~12 months from Jan 2026), initial readiness targeted early 2027; phase 3 to open launch services to international customers
note: Equatorial site on land allocated to Turkey under a bilateral agreement; exact location, vehicles and costs not disclosed. Targets LEO and GEO; three phases from national use to international commercial service.

name: Spaceport Kii
note: Japan's first private spaceport (Canon, IHI, Shimizu backing). Kairos 0/3: Mar 2024, Dec 2024, Mar 2026 all failed; no date for flight 4. Band from Kairos reference orbits (33 deg, 97 deg); all flights aimed at 97.5 deg SSO (GCAT).

name: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), Sriharikota
active_vehicles: GSLV Mk II (ISRO), LVM3 (ISRO), PSLV (ISRO), SSLV (ISRO), Vikram-1 (Skyroot Aerospace)
planned_vehicles: Agnibaan (AgniKul Cosmos), NGLV (Next Generation Launch Vehicle) (ISRO), Vikram-2 (Skyroot Aerospace)
orbits: GTO, HEO, LEO, lunar, polar, SSO
expansion: Third Launch Pad approved Jan 2025 (Rs 3,985 crore, ~4 yrs, for NGLV/LVM3, standby for SLP); SLP upgraded for Gaganyaan; PIF (2024) raises FLP cadence
note: Inclination band = achieved 2010-26 (GCAT); SSO needs a payload-costly dogleg. Foreign payloads fly via NSIL, no foreign launchers. Private: Skyroot Vikram-1 reached orbit from FLP 18 Jul 2026; Agnikul has own pad ALP-01 Dhanush. Pads: FLP, SLP, ALP-01.

name: SpaceX Starbase (Boca Chica)
expansion: OLP-1 being rebuilt for Starship V3 (OLP-2 active since 2026); Giga Bay; 'Starpipe' methane pipeline due Jan 2027. Separate Starbase Louisiana site from 2029.
note: Starship test and production site. Flights head east over the Gulf/Florida Straits, so only low inclinations (~26°+, max not published); no polar. GCAT counts Starship test flights as orbital launches (2023 first).

name: Starbase Louisiana (Vermilion Parish)
expansion: 10 Starship pads (5 complexes × 2), construction from end-2027, first launch as soon as 2029; ≥US$100B investment (announced 25 Aug 2026).
note: Coordinates are an estimate (Pecan Island area, ~125,000 acres). Still needs environmental, wetlands and launch approvals. Orbits not published; Gulf coast suggests low inclinations only (inferred).

name: Space Hub Sutherland (A' Mhòine)
operator: Highlands and Islands Enterprise (asset owner since Aug 2026); no launch operator
expansion: None scheduled. HIE bought Sutherland Spaceport Ltd assets from Orbex liquidators (Aug 2026) and is reviewing options; no launch provider named.
note: Construction halted Dec 2024 (only ~600 m access road built); Orbex, the sole tenant, ceased operations Feb 2026. Wikipedia lists 90° (polar); azimuth band not published, so inclinations left null.

name: Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center
operator: PLA Aerospace Force (Taiyuan SLC); CASC listed as operator
active_vehicles: Long March 2C (CASC), Long March 2D (CASC), Long March 4B (CASC), Long March 6 (CASC), Long March 6A (CASC), Long March 6C (CASC)
expansion: CZ-6C added at LC-9A (2024); CZ-6A cadence rising (10 launches 2025); oversees Oriental sea-launch spaceport
note: China's main SSO/polar site (13/12/12 launches 2024/25/26). Pads LC-9, 9A, 16 plus a mobile pad (Kuaizhou). Inclinations observed (GCAT), max incl. retrograde 142° Yaogan-50 (2026); min = latitude (38.0° observed). Inland, debris over land.

name: Tanegashima Space Center
expansion: LA-Y1 (ex-H-IIA) planned to be adapted for H3; H3 cadence rising (3 flights Jun-Oct 2026)
note: Japan's main site. Inclination band = achieved 2015-26 (GCAT). H-IIA retired after F50 (28 Jun 2025). H3 F8 failed Dec 2025 (QZS-5), back to flight Jun 2026. Only national vehicles (JAXA/MHI). Also hosts Epsilon S motor tests.

name: Uchinoura Space Center
expansion: Epsilon S return to flight targeted FY2026-27, now with older M-35a second stage after test explosions in 2023 and 2024
note: No orbital launch since Epsilon F6 failure (Oct 2022); site active for sounding rockets and balloons. Inclination band estimated (latitude to SSO flown by Epsilon). Formerly Kagoshima Space Center (GCAT KASC).

name: Vandenberg Space Force Base
operator: U.S. Space Force (Space Launch Delta 30, Western Range)
active_vehicles: Alpha (Firefly Aerospace), Falcon 9 (Block 5) (SpaceX), Minotaur IV (Northrop Grumman)
planned_vehicles: Daytona (Phantom Space), Eclipse (Firefly/Northrop Grumman MLV) (Firefly Aerospace), Falcon Heavy (SpaceX), New Glenn (Blue Origin), Vulcan Centaur (United Launch Alliance)
providers: Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Northrop Grumman, Phantom Space, SpaceX, United Launch Alliance
expansion: SLC-6 conversion for Falcon 9/Heavy (up to 5 FH/yr); SLC-3E Vulcan (planned); SLC-14 Blue Origin New Glenn (leased); SLC-5 Phantom Daytona (leased); Firefly Eclipse at SLC-2W; >$800M range modernisation over 5 yrs.
note: Main US polar/SSO site (Transporter rideshares). 147–201° azimuths give 63–107° direct (computed); min 53° reflects Starlink missions flown with doglegs (team knowledge, unverified). Coastal Commission objected to cadence rise; harbour usable ~30% of time.

name: Vostochny Cosmodrome
expansion: Angara A5 from Site 1A since Apr 2024; crewed Angara-A5P/Orel flights planned from Site 1A (2028+); Amur pad (2A) and super-heavy pad planned
note: Civil cosmodrome meant to reduce reliance on Baikonur. Low cadence: 4 (2024), 2 (2025), 0 (2026 to date). Mainly SSO incl. Glavkosmos Soyuz rideshares. Nov 2025 contractor power cut/bankruptcy hit unfinished areas only.

name: Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport (Wallops Island)
operator: Virginia Spaceport Authority (on NASA Wallops Flight Facility)
planned_vehicles: Alpha (Firefly Aerospace), Antares 330 (Northrop Grumman), Eclipse (Firefly/Northrop Grumman MLV) (Firefly Aerospace), Neutron (Rocket Lab)
providers: Firefly Aerospace, Northrop Grumman, Rocket Lab
expansion: Rocket Lab LC-3 for Neutron opened Aug 2025 (first launch NET 2027); Northrop Antares 330 (NG-22, 2027) and Firefly/Northrop Eclipse from LP-0A; Firefly Alpha from LP-0A (NASA INCUS, 2027).
note: Wikipedia labels 38–60° as approved azimuth range; values match an inclination band (38° ≈ site latitude), used here as inclinations. 1995 = first MARS pad launch (Conestoga); NASA Scout flew orbital from Wallops in the 1960s. LP-0A idle since Aug 2023.

name: Wenchang Space Launch Site
operator: CASC / PLA Aerospace Force (state launch site)
active_vehicles: Long March 5 (CASC), Long March 5B (CASC), Long March 7 (CASC), Long March 7A (CASC), Long March 8 (CASC), Long March 8A (CASC)
expansion: LC-301 for Long March 10/10A: Mengzhou abort test 11 Feb 2026; uncrewed lunar test 2027, crewed lunar landing 2028–29
note: Coastal, China's lowest latitude (19.6°N): heavy GTO, lunar, Tiangong cargo, station modules (6/12/6 launches 2024/25/26). Min incl. = latitude; GTO to ~14° via plane change. SSO flown by CZ-8 (2020, 2022). Super-heavy = planned CZ-10.

name: Whalers Way Orbital Launch Complex
expansion: Two pads for polar/SSO planned; Native Vegetation Council refused required heritage-agreement change (Sept 2026), halting construction.
note: Only one suborbital test (TiSPACE Hapith I, 2021, failed at ignition). Conservation area, opposition from environmental groups and traditional owners. Southern Launch now flies suborbital from Koonibba. Inclination figures not published.

name: Xichang Satellite Launch Center
operator: PLA Aerospace Force (27th Experimental Training Base); CASC listed as operator
active_vehicles: Kuaizhou-1A (ExPace (CASIC)), Long March 2C (CASC), Long March 2D (CASC), Long March 3B/E (CASC), Long March 3C/E (CASC), Long March 4B (CASC), Long March 4C (CASC)
orbits: escape, GTO, HEO, LEO, MEO, SSO
expansion: New pad for next-generation rockets (e.g. CZ-8) reported under construction (2019); Kuaizhou-1A flies from LC-4 since 2022
note: China's main GTO/BeiDou site (18/18/6 launches 2024/25/26). Inland: spent stages repeatedly fall near villages (incidents Dec 2023, Jun 2024). Min incl. = latitude; GTO missions reach ~17.6° via plane change. SSO rare (GF-14).

name: Yangjiang sea launch area (South China Sea)
operator: Sea-launch zone off Yangjiang, Guangdong; operating launch centre not confirmed
note: Sea-launch zone, not a fixed pad: 6 orbital launches 2023–26 (GCAT) incl. Gravity-1 maiden flight (Jan 2024) and Jielong-3; only SSO inclination recorded (97.3°, CZ-11 2023). Launch counts 2/0/2 (2024/25/26).

name: Yasny launch base (Dombarovsky)
operator: Strategic Rocket Forces (Dnepr launches marketed by Kosmotras)
note: ICBM base; 10 Dnepr (converted R-36M silo ICBM) orbital launches 2006–2015, none since (GCAT). Coords = silo 370/13. polar_sso from past SSO payloads (e.g. KOMPSAT-3A); vehicle class an estimate. Still used for ICBM/Avangard tests.
